neighbours.label: 'to' in 'something / nothing / anything to <verb>': an infinitive naming what there is to act on
fire: After the factory closed, the young men in town had nothing to do all day.
Bring a book so the kids have something to read on the train.
Without a clear goal, the team had nothing to aim for.
The detectives had little to go on except a muddy footprint.
She always finds something to complain about at dinner.
Is there anything to eat in the fridge?
The new rules give us a framework to work within.
We finally had something to celebrate after a long season.
quiet: After the factory closed, many young men moved to the city.
Bring a book when the kids go to their grandmother's house.
Without a clear goal, the team decided to rest for a week.
The detectives drove to the farm before sunrise.
She always talks to her sister at dinner.
Is the fridge connected to the generator?
The new rules apply to every member of staff.
We finally went to the stadium after a long season.

notes: - pole (not tested): the subject inside a relative clause after 'everything' (everything she eats).
